title: Zuga of Chadayyav

paragraphs: [Niddah 21b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.21b.14), and [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Niddah.21b.14.3) explains: two Torah scholars from that place; and in [Tosafot](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosafot_on_Niddah.21b.14.1) the explanation, from the Arukh, is that Zuza is the name of a sage. And in [Jerusalem Talmud Demai 2:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Demai.2.1.9): Rabbi Mana said, I went to Caesarea — I asked Rabbi Yitzchak bar Elazar, and he said to me, "Thus Zuga practiced" — Rabbi Yitzchak ben Elazar also transmitted a ruling in the name of Zuga of Caesarea.

notes.text: The Gemara has Zuga of Chadayyav. Rashi takes the word to mean two scholars, while Tosafot cites the Arukh in reading Zuza as one sage’s name. In the linked Demai passage, Mana asks Rabbi Yitzchak bar Elazar directly, and Rabbi Yitzchak separately transmits a ruling in the name of Zuga of Caesarea.
